18	The Defendants contend that the Complaint should be dismissed in its entirety for failure to comply with the 2004 Agreement’s dispute resolution and mediation clause. L.P./Inc. Mot. to Dismiss at 12-13. The clause provides that “[a]ny dispute, controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof shall first be referred by the parties to their senior-level executives for attempted resolution through good-faith negotiations.” Compl. Ex. A § 9.1 (emphasis added). Should negotiations fail, thirty days after making a written request to initiate those negotiations, “either Party may, by written notice to the other, require that the Dispute be referred to non-binding mediation administered by the American Arbitration Association.” Id. Skold responds that the language of the mediation clause is permissive (“either Party may ... require”) and also argues that, in any event, Inc. has waived its right to invoke the clause because it participated in litigation over the dispute in the cancellation action before the TTAB. 19	The dispute resolution clause in the 2004 Agreement contains two clauses, one of which is mandatory (the parties shall refer the matter to senior executives to attempt to negotiate a resolution) and the other which is permissive (the parties may refer the matter to nonbinding mediation). 20	L.P. and S.A., who are not parties to the 2004 Agreement, also contend that the dispute resolution clause requires their dismissal from this action. In essence, they urge this Court to accept the contention that a nonparty to an agreement should be permitted to force a signatory party to engage in negotiations pursuant to a permissive mediation clause in that agreement as a condition precedent to filing suit but cite no relevant case or statute in support of this contention. See United States v. Benish, 5 F.3d 20, 26 (3d Cir.1993) (rejecting a party’s claim where the party “provided] no legal support for his argument or any persuasive reason” for the court to find in his favor). The Court sees no persuasive reason to dismiss Skold’s entire Complaint based on this unsupported argument. Accordingly, the motion to dismiss the Complaint against L.P. and S.A. on this ground shall be denied.
21	Regarding Inc.: although Skold did fail to bring in a senior-level executive to try to resolve the dispute — as he was required to do under the dispute resolution provision — Inc.’s participation in the TTAB proceedings waived any rights it may have had to seek to have the parties’ executives negotiate an end to the dispute. See, e.g., LBL Skysystems (USA), Inc. v. APG-Am., Inc., No. 02-5379, 2005 WL 2140240, at *30 (E.D.Pa. Aug. 31, 2005) (holding that a “party that engages in discovery and files pretrial motions waives a contract’s alternative dispute resolution provision”); Smith v. IMG Worldwide, Inc., 360 F.Supp.2d 681, 687 (E.D.Pa.2005) (finding that a party’s engaging in motion practice and providing “substantial discovery” constituted waiver of contractual alternative dispute resolution provision).
22	Viewing the four years’ worth of docket entries in the TTAB action, the Court considers that Inc. did not file a motion to stay the TTAB proceedings pending executive-level negotiations and instead filed, inter alia, motions to dismiss, a protective order, multiple summary judgment motions (one of which was partially granted in its favor), and a final brief in preparation for trial. See, e.g., Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897, 2012 WL 5902083 (T.T.A.B. Nov. 8, 2012) (granting Inc.’s motion for partial summary judgment on Skold’s abandonment claim). See also generally Registrant’s Trial Brief, Sköld v. Galderma Labs., Inc., Cancellation No. 92052897 (T.T.A.B. Aug. 13, 2014), Docket No. 81. This four-year history of litigation in the cancellation action — from filing nearly through trial — is, on its face, inconsistent with the notion that Inc. was willing to engage in the good-faith executive-level negotiations required by the dispute resolution provision.
23	Moreover, the Court can look to the TTAB’s grant of partial summary judgment in favor of Inc. and dismissing Skold’s abandonment claim as a concrete example of an instance where Inc.’s conduct inconsistent with the dispute resolution clause caused prejudice to Skold, not to mention the expenditure of time, cost, and resources attendant to maintaining a multi-year trademark cancellation action. 12	International ACH and Wire Transactions If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved, and the laws enforced by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (“OFAC”). Under such rules and laws, we may temporarily suspend processing of a transaction for greater scrutiny or verification against the OFAC list of blocked parties, which may result in delayed settlement, posting and/or availability of funds. If we determine there is a violation, or if we cannot satisfactorily resolve a suspected or potential violation, the subject funds will be blocked as required by law. If you believe you have adequate grounds to seek the return of any blocked funds, it is your sole responsibility to pursue the matter with the appropriate governmental authorities. Please see the OFAC website for procedures and form required to seek a release of blocked funds.

19	shall continue in force for a one (1) year period, and shall be automatically renewed for additional one (1) year periods thereafter unless terminated by written notice from either party to the other party not less than sixty (60) days prior to the end of the initial or any subsequent one (1) year term.

21	The termination provision, on its face, provides a comprehensive account of the ways in which the Agreement may be terminated. There is no indication in the Agreement that the parties contemplated that the House Accounts provision would constitute an additional means for terminating all of Lovejoy’s obligations under the Agreement. This interpretation would allow Lovejoy to escape from all of its obligations under the Agreement and all of the restrictions in the termination provision.

In other words, the “mutual” termination provision would never apply to Lovejoy.

{"clause_id":"c240","reasoning_cat1":"A short three-component formula; mechanical.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Principal Funds, Extra Principal Distribution Amount and Overcollateralization Release Amount definitions and Section 6.04.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c241","reasoning_cat1":"A very long compound definition with a missing conjunction between limbs (d) and (e), a mis-set enumerator, and a residual 'or as otherwise set forth in this Agreement' deduction.","reasoning_cat2":"Limb (e) cites 'Section 2.03(d)' for substitutions, but Section 2.03 of this Agreement has only subsections (a) and (b) and the substitution mechanics sit in unlettered paragraphs, so the cross-reference does not land.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.34},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c280","reasoning_cat1":"Condition (ii) — 'have a fixed Mortgage Rate not less than or more than 1% per annum higher than the Mortgage Rate of the Deleted Mortgage Loan' — is grammatically broken and leaves the permitted rate band genuinely uncertain, and (iii) uses the undefined comparative 'same or higher credit quality characteristics'.","reasoning_cat2":"Condition (ix) requires compliance with 'each representation and warranty set forth in Section 2.03 hereof', but Section 2.03 of this Agreement contains only the Master Servicer's and Securities Administrator's corporate representations, not loan-level warranties — those live in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement and Bring Down Agreements.","prob_cat1":0.40,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c281","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.18 supplies the content; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c282","reasoning_cat1":"'Substantially in the form of Exhibit G' plus a deemed-execution rule for electronic delivery; the closing 'of the related Servicer, as applicable' is a dangling qualifier.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.02, 2.03 and 4.07, which condition release of Mortgage Files on a Request for Release.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c283","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line definition whose entire content is a cross-reference to 'Section 6.08 hereof'.","reasoning_cat2":"The Reserve Fund is in fact established under Section 4.22(b) ('the Securities Administrator shall establish a Reserve Fund'), while Section 6.08 is the Class P Certificate Account; the pointer contradicts the operative provision.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c284","reasoning_cat1":"States a fixed $5,000 amount; clear on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"It again cites Section 6.08, but Section 4.22(b) is the provision that requires the Depositor to cause the Reserve Fund Deposit to be deposited; the cross-reference is wrong.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.39},
{"clause_id":"c285","reasoning_cat1":"Describes each listed certificate as 'evidencing the sole class of Residual Interests in the related REMIC', which does not fit the Class RX Certificate representing three separate residual interests.","reasoning_cat2":"Read with c100, c107 and c343, the treatment of the Class RX Certificate is workable but the singular formulation is loose.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c286","reasoning_cat1":"Statutory incorporation; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c285 and the Preliminary Statement.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c287","reasoning_cat1":"After enumerating specific offices it sweeps in 'any other officer customarily performing functions similar to those performed by any of the above designated officers or other officers of the Trustee specified by the Trustee' — a general catch-all whose reach determines when the Trustee is charged with knowledge.","reasoning_cat2":"This term controls the Trustee's knowledge-based duties in Article X; nothing contradicts it, but its breadth interacts with those duties.","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c288","reasoning_cat1":"Names a rating agency; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Rating Agency definition.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c289","reasoning_cat1":"Names an entity; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Servicer definition and the Saxon agreements.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c290","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies a specific dated agreement; determinate on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"It says the agreement is 'attached hereto as Exhibit R-3', but the Wells Fargo Assignment Agreement (c345) is also said to be Exhibit R-3, and no Exhibit R-2 is used — two different documents claim the same exhibit.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c291","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies a specific dated agreement and exhibit; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c290 and the Servicing Agreement definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c292","reasoning_cat1":"Short and determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"The instrument elsewhere uses the undefined 'Monthly Payment' (c203, c248) where this term was evidently meant; the mismatch is between those provisions, not this one.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c293","reasoning_cat1":"Statutory reference; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the transfer restrictions in Section 7.02.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.03},
{"clause_id":"c294","reasoning_cat1":"Names the entity in three capacities; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"It says Wells Fargo acts as paying agent, which duplicates the separate Paying Agent definition (c228); harmless overlap.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c296","reasoning_cat1":"'Any of EMC and the Sponsor' is awkward but the class of two is clear.","reasoning_cat2":"The Agreement elsewhere uses 'the Sellers' collectively and 'the related Seller' distributively (Sections 2.01-2.03) without saying which of EMC or the Sponsor sold which loans.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c297","reasoning_cat1":"Closed three-item list.","reasoning_cat2":"Wells Fargo is here a Servicer while also being Master Servicer and Securities Administrator; c344 resolves this by defining 'Wells Fargo' in its servicer capacity, but the overlap runs through Sections 4.03 and 6.02.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c298","reasoning_cat1":"Uses the open standard 'customary, reasonable and necessary' followed by 'including, but not limited to' and a four-item list, and closes by referring to 'Nonrecoverable Servicing Advances', a term this Agreement never defines.","reasoning_cat2":"The undefined term has to be filled from the Nonrecoverable Advance definition (c211) or the Servicing Agreements; the Liquidation Proceeds definition also deducts Servicing Advances, so the boundary matters to the waterfall.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c299","reasoning_cat1":"Closed three-item list.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c116, c291 and the Wells Fargo Servicing Agreement definition.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c300","reasoning_cat1":"Adds to a fixed regulatory list an open alternative — criteria 'otherwise mutually agreed to ... in response to evolving interpretations of Regulation AB and incorporated into a revised Exhibit N' — with no standard for what counts.","reasoning_cat2":"It permits a de facto amendment of Exhibit N by four named parties, which sits alongside the amendment provisions of Section 12.01 and the compliance obligations of Section 4.17.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.25},
{"clause_id":"c301","reasoning_cat1":"A clean per-loan fee formula.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Servicing Fee Rate, Net Mortgage Rate and Interest Funds definitions; note it contains no float-income add-on, unlike the parallel Master Servicing Fee (c186).","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c302","reasoning_cat1":"A single number.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c301 and the Mortgage Loan Schedule item (u), though the Schedule contemplates a per-loan Servicing Fee Rate while this fixes one rate for all loans.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c303","reasoning_cat1":"Garbled — 'involved in, or responsible for, the administration and servicing of the Mortgage Loans in the case of the related Servicer, as to which evidence reasonably acceptable to the Trustee, as applicable, of due authorization, by such party has been furnished' — the syntax obscures whose authorization is required.","reasoning_cat2":"It is used in the Officer's Certificate and Request for Release definitions; no contradiction, but the evidentiary condition is not repeated there.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c304","reasoning_cat1":"Rests entirely on 'the reasonable good-faith estimate by EMC or its affiliate' of an aggregate 'Maximum Probable Exposure', itself an undefined internal methodology.","reasoning_cat2":"It inherits the vagueness of the Maximum Probable Exposure definition (c190) and drives the Significance Percentage (c305) and the Regulation AB disclosure obligations in Section 4.18.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c305","reasoning_cat1":"A clean ratio, though its numerator is the soft Significance Estimate.","reasoning_cat2":"Depends on c304 and c190; the chain of vagueness is inherited rather than created here.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c306","reasoning_cat1":"A precise dollar amount with an explanation of what it represents.","reasoning_cat2":"It is a Trust Fund asset under c335 and is added into balances in c122, c209, c223 and c241; the treatment is consistent.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c307","reasoning_cat1":"Names the entity, its predecessor and its capacity; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"The Sponsor is the party carrying the Section 2.02(d) backstop repurchase obligation for Accredited-originated loans; the definition itself is consistent.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c308","reasoning_cat1":"One line; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Closing Date definition and Section 4.02's REMIC covenants.","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c309","reasoning_cat1":"Limb (i) deducts principal 'due with respect to such Mortgage Loan during each Due Period' without saying 'each Due Period ended prior to the relevant Distribution Date', leaving the cut-off implicit.","reasoning_cat2":"It is the workhorse input for the Overcollateralization, Trigger Event, Net Rate Cap and Principal Distribution Amount definitions, all of which assume a fixed as-of date; the implicit cut-off has to be supplied from those.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c310","reasoning_cat1":"A nested later-of/earlier-of test with specific dates and a specific percentage; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Current Specified Enhancement Percentage (c118) and the Overcollateralization Target Amount (c225).","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c311","reasoning_cat1":"A closed list.","reasoning_cat2":"It groups the Residual Certificates with the subordinated classes even though they have no Certificate Principal Balance and take no loss allocation under Section 6.05; the grouping is loose.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c312","reasoning_cat1":"The syntax collapses — 'amounts received ... or surplus amounts held ... to cover estimated expenses (including ... recoveries in respect of the representations and warranties made by the Seller) specifically related to a Mortgage Loan that was the subject of a liquidation or final disposition of any REO Property' — so it is unclear what the parenthetical modifies.","reasoning_cat2":"It nets expenses 'permitted to be reimbursed pursuant to Section 6.05', but Section 6.05 is the allocation of Realized Losses rather than an expense-reimbursement provision; and treating repurchase-warranty recoveries as Subsequent Recoveries sits against the Purchase Price mechanics of Sections 2.02 and 2.03.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.33},
{"clause_id":"c313","reasoning_cat1":"Short and determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Servicing Agreements and Section 4.03.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c314","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference.","reasoning_cat2":"It points to 'Section 2.03(d)', but Section 2.03 of this Agreement has only subsections (a) and (b) — the Substitution Adjustment Amount is actually defined in an unlettered paragraph of Section 2.03(a); the citation does not land.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.36},
{"clause_id":"c315","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference.","reasoning_cat2":"It points to Section 9.01 (Events of Default), whereas the table of contents places 'Successor Master Servicer' at Section 8.06; the two cannot both be the source.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c316","reasoning_cat1":"A closed description of the trust corpus with an express 'for the avoidance of doubt' exclusion; internally clear.","reasoning_cat2":"It states that the Swap Administration Agreement does not form part of the Trust Fund, yet the Trust Fund definition (c335) expressly includes as item (vi) 'the rights under the Swap Administration Agreement relating to the Certificates' — a direct contradiction between two Article I definitions.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.46},
{"clause_id":"c317","reasoning_cat1":"A long but conventional successor-and-merger formulation, ending with a redundant tail.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.22(a), which gives the Supplemental Interest Trust Trustee the Securities Administrator's rights and protections.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c318","reasoning_cat1":"Short and determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.22(a) says the Swap Account shall be an Eligible Account held within the Supplemental Interest Trust; consistent, though this definition makes the Swap Administrator rather than the Securities Administrator its maintainer.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c319","reasoning_cat1":"One line; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.22(c) and the Swap Administration Agreement definition.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c320","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies the agreement functionally rather than by parties, and allows amendment 'from time to time'.","reasoning_cat2":"It is not attached as an exhibit, unlike the Swap Agreement (Exhibit M-1), yet it governs payments to Certificateholders under Section 4.22.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c321","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies the agreement and its annexes; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"The Notional Amount definition (c212) refers to a schedule 'set forth in Exhibit M' while this attaches the Swap Agreement as 'Exhibit M-1'; the exhibit references do not quite match.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c322","reasoning_cat1":"Short and determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c316 and Section 4.22(a).","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c323","reasoning_cat1":"Short and determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c321, which already sweeps credit support annexes into the Swap Agreement; note the table of contents also lists a 'Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex' at Section 5.04.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c324","reasoning_cat1":"Incorporates a Swap Agreement term; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Swap Termination Payment definition.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c325","reasoning_cat1":"Incorporates two Swap Agreement terms; clear, though its content is wholly extrinsic.","reasoning_cat2":"Swap LIBOR drives the REMIC I and REMIC II pass-through rate tables (c340, c341), so an extrinsic definition determines internal REMIC arithmetic.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c326","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 11.01 supplies the content; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c327","reasoning_cat1":"Names the initial provider with a functional definition; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.22 and the Swap Provider Trigger Event definition.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c328","reasoning_cat1":"Three enumerated Swap Agreement events, each defined there; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Affected Party and Defaulting Party definitions and Section 4.22(c)'s subordination of trigger-event termination payments.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c329","reasoning_cat1":"Two-directional definition; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.22(c) and the Interest Funds and Principal Funds deductions.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c330","reasoning_cat1":"Three sentences that each do different work — designation, identification of who holds the role, and appointment of an agent; clear enough.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.02's REMIC administration covenants.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c331","reasoning_cat1":"Pure cross-reference.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 7.02(c) supplies the content; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.05},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c346","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies a dated agreement 'in substantially the form of Exhibit J-2'; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"It names 'the Seller' in the singular while c296 defines two Sellers; the parallel Deutsche Bank Custodial Agreement (c136) instead names the Depositor, EMC and the Sponsor.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c347","reasoning_cat1":"Identifies specific dated agreements and an exhibit; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c299 and c345, save that c345's exhibit numbering collides with the Saxon Assignment Agreement.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c348","reasoning_cat1":"Names an entity; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Bring Down Agreements definition (c040).","prob_cat1":0.02,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c349","reasoning_cat1":"The text is truncated — 'the cap contract, dated Agreement Provider' omits both the date and the counterparty, so the instrument being defined is not fully identified on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"It is nonetheless anchored to Exhibit M-2 and used throughout Sections 4.22 and 5.04 and the Trust Fund definition; the gap must be filled from those.","prob_cat1":0.33,"prob_cat2":0.21},
{"clause_id":"c350","reasoning_cat1":"Names the initial provider with a functional definition; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.22(b), which requires deposit into the Reserve Fund of all payments received from this provider.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c351","reasoning_cat1":"A single fixed date; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the yield maintenance mechanics of Section 4.22(b) and the June 2008 switch in the REMIC rate tables.","prob_cat1":0.03,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c352","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line cross-reference definition.","reasoning_cat2":"It points to Section 5.04, which the table of contents titles 'Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex' rather than an account-creation section; the pointer may not land, in contrast with the Distribution Account's dangling 'Section 5.08'.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c353","reasoning_cat1":"Short and determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"It is between the Securities Administrator and the provider, whereas the Swap Credit Support Annex (c323) is between the Supplemental Interest Trust Trustee and the Swap Provider; the asymmetry is deliberate but unexplained.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c354","reasoning_cat1":"Three long parallel allocation rules with fixed 98%/2% splits and pro rata mechanics; dense but each step is determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"It supplies the allocation that the Current Interest (c117) and Uncertificated Accrued Interest (c337) definitions cross-refer to; the three tiers line up with the REMIC structure.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c355","reasoning_cat1":"Contains real textual defects — 'the assets in the Mortgage Loans', a certification to be made by 'the Seller or the title Servicer issuing the commitment for title insurance' (evidently the title insurer), and a first enumerator rendered '(1)' — in the provision that effects the conveyance and fixes the delivery requirements.","reasoning_cat2":"Its document list is the referent for the Mortgage File definition (c199) and for the Custodian's certifications in Sections 2.02(a) and (b), which expressly limit review of 'subclauses (iv) and (vi) of Section 2.01'; the title-policy limb permits delivery up to a year after closing, which sits awkwardly with the 180-day Final Certification.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c356","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed certification mechanics with a conclusive-reliance clause; the phrase 'appear to be defective on its face' is a judgment standard but a workable one, and 'the Sponsor, the Sellers, the Trustee' is missing a conjunction.","reasoning_cat2":"It carves out subclauses (iv) and (vi) of Section 2.01, and its exception-report output feeds the cure/repurchase mechanic in Section 2.02(c); consistent.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c357","reasoning_cat1":"Parallel to (a) with a 180-day deadline; the 'appear defective on its face' standard again requires judgment but the mechanics are clear.","reasoning_cat2":"The Final Certification requires evidence of recording, yet Section 2.01 clause (x) expressly contemplates documents still out for recording, so the two must be reconciled in practice.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c358","reasoning_cat1":"The closing sentence says 'The obligation ... to cure, repurchase or substitute ... shall be the sole remedies respecting such defect available to the Certificateholders or to the Securities Administrator on their behalf' — a singular obligation described as plural 'remedies', and a sole-remedy clause whose reach ('such defect') is not defined.","reasoning_cat2":"It names only the Certificateholders and the Securities Administrator, omitting the Trustee, who is the party charged by Section 2.02(d) with enforcing repurchase obligations — so it is unclear whether the sole-remedy limitation binds the Trustee's enforcement action.","prob_cat1":0.42,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c359","reasoning_cat1":"A short but heavily loaded provision: it obliges the Trustee to enforce not only repurchase but 'any other obligations of the related Seller or the related Originator under such agreements, including, without limitation, the obligation of the Sponsor to repurchase ... any Mortgage Loan originated by Accredited in the event that Accredited fails' — a general catch-all followed by one named specific, leaving the backstop's scope and trigger ('fails to repurchase') open.","reasoning_cat2":"It has to be squared with Section 2.02(c)'s sole-remedy sentence, with the Purchase Price definition (c246) which covers only Section 2.02 repurchases, and with the repurchase machinery in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement and Bring Down Agreements that this Agreement only incorporates by reference.","prob_cat1":0.56,"prob_cat2":0.55},
{"clause_id":"c360","reasoning_cat1":"The section is headed as the Master Servicer's and Securities Administrator's representations but its later paragraphs impose an unrelated notice-of-breach duty ('shall give prompt written notice thereof to the other parties') and the whole substitution and Purchase Price mechanic; 'prompt' and 'materially and adversely affects' are both open standards.","reasoning_cat2":"Several other provisions cite 'Section 2.03(b)(v)' (c200), 'Section 2.03(d)' (c241, c314) and 'the representations and warranties set forth in Section 2.03' (c280, c364) as if this section contained loan-level warranties and lettered subsections it does not have.","prob_cat1":0.40,"prob_cat2":0.47},
{"clause_id":"c361","reasoning_cat1":"A single-sentence survival clause; clear in itself.","reasoning_cat2":"It makes 'the representations and warranties set forth in Section 2.03' survive delivery of the Mortgage Loans, but Section 2.03's representations are Wells Fargo's corporate representations, which have nothing to do with delivery of Mortgage Files — and other provisions cite a non-existent Section 2.03(b)(v).","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c362","reasoning_cat1":"Contains the ungrammatical 'Upon discovery by the Depositor, the Trustee of a breach' (missing conjunction), 'validly existing as limited liability company', and a mis-set subclause '(4)'; the good-title representation is otherwise clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Its notice duty runs to 'the other parties to this Agreement and to each Rating Agency', while the parallel duty in Section 2.03 omits the Rating Agencies — an unexplained asymmetry between two adjacent notice provisions.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c363","reasoning_cat1":"'Not in default or as to which default is not reasonably foreseeable' is a forward-looking standard, but the tax conditions it protects are precisely cited.","reasoning_cat2":"It opens 'Notwithstanding any contrary provision of this Agreement' and so overrides the repurchase timing in Sections 2.02 and 2.03, which is expressly acknowledged in Section 2.03's Purchase Price paragraph.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c364","reasoning_cat1":"Gives the Seller or Originator an option among cure, substitution and repurchase within 90 days; the mechanics are clear though 'discovery' is undefined.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires the Securities Administrator (not the Trustee) to reconvey the loan, while everywhere else the Custodian acts 'on behalf of the Trustee', and it points to substitution conditions 'in Section 2.03', which contains no lettered substitution conditions.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c365","reasoning_cat1":"An acknowledgement and declaration of trust; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.01's conveyance and Section 7.01's issuance of the Certificates.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c366","reasoning_cat1":"A conveyance in trust; the OCR renders 'REMIC II' inconsistently but the sense is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC II recital (c005) and c367.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c367","reasoning_cat1":"A conveyance in trust with a matched acknowledgement; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC III recital (c007) and the Class CE, P and IO Interest definitions.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c368","reasoning_cat1":"A conveyance in trust; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC IV definition (c270) and c107.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c369","reasoning_cat1":"A conveyance in trust; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC V definition (c271) and c107.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c370","reasoning_cat1":"A conveyance in trust; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC VI definition (c272), though the beneficiaries are 'holders of REMIC VI Regular Interest IO', an interest c015 says is held by the Supplemental Interest Trust.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c371","reasoning_cat1":"The list is not grammatically parallel ('(a) acquire and hold' against '(b) to issue'), limb (d) is an open catch-all for anything 'necessary, suitable or convenient', and the final sentence trails off with 'and this Section 2.07'.","reasoning_cat2":"The purpose limitation has to be squared with the Trust's participation in the Swap and Yield Maintenance arrangements under Section 4.22, which are not among the enumerated purposes.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c372","reasoning_cat1":"A very long duty provision built on open standards — 'anything which it may deem necessary or desirable', 'consult with the Servicers as necessary' — but the specific reconciliation and notification duties are concrete.","reasoning_cat2":"Its 'Accepted Master Servicing Practices' standard (c019) and its enforcement duty overlap with Section 4.03(b), which states the enforcement obligation in different and more demanding terms.","prob_cat1":0.22,"prob_cat2":0.23},
{"clause_id":"c373","reasoning_cat1":"Three specific prohibitions with defined exceptions; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Limb (b) excepts substitutions 'pursuant to the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement or Section 2.03 of this Agreement', consistent with Section 2.03's two-year substitution cut-off and Section 2.05's opinion requirement.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c374","reasoning_cat1":"Turns on the Master Servicer's own 'judgment' and on what it 'deems appropriate', and permits reliance on the Servicer's own Officer's Certificate as to its own compliance.","reasoning_cat2":"The carve-out for Wells Fargo as Servicer here dovetails with Section 4.03(b), which routes Wells Fargo terminations through the Trustee; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c375","reasoning_cat1":"Long and layered, with a 'good faith business judgment ... were it the owner of the related Mortgage Loans' standard, an indemnity precondition on prosecuting claims, and the stray 'Successor master Servicer'.","reasoning_cat2":"It splits enforcement between the Master Servicer and the Trustee depending on whether Wells Fargo is the defaulting Servicer, which must be read with Section 4.01's general enforcement duty and Sections 8.06/9.01 on successors — the indemnity precondition also sits against the Trustee's Article X duties.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.28},

{"clause_id":"c352","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line cross-reference definition.","reasoning_cat2":"It points to Section 5.04, which the table of contents titles 'Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex' rather than an account-creation section; the pointer may not land, in contrast with the Distribution Account's dangling 'Section 5.08'.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c353","reasoning_cat1":"Short and determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"It is between the Securities Administrator and the provider, whereas the Swap Credit Support Annex (c323) is between the Supplemental Interest Trust Trustee and the Swap Provider; the asymmetry is deliberate but unexplained.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c354","reasoning_cat1":"Three long parallel allocation rules with fixed 98%/2% splits and pro rata mechanics; dense but each step is determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"It supplies the allocation that the Current Interest (c117) and Uncertificated Accrued Interest (c337) definitions cross-refer to; the three tiers line up with the REMIC structure.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c355","reasoning_cat1":"Contains real textual defects — 'the assets in the Mortgage Loans', a certification to be made by 'the Seller or the title Servicer issuing the commitment for title insurance' (evidently the title insurer), and a first enumerator rendered '(1)' — in the provision that effects the conveyance and fixes the delivery requirements.","reasoning_cat2":"Its document list is the referent for the Mortgage File definition (c199) and for the Custodian's certifications in Sections 2.02(a) and (b), which expressly limit review of 'subclauses (iv) and (vi) of Section 2.01'; the title-policy limb permits delivery up to a year after closing, which sits awkwardly with the 180-day Final Certification.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c356","reasoning_cat1":"Detailed certification mechanics with a conclusive-reliance clause; the phrase 'appear to be defective on its face' is a judgment standard but a workable one, and 'the Sponsor, the Sellers, the Trustee' is missing a conjunction.","reasoning_cat2":"It carves out subclauses (iv) and (vi) of Section 2.01, and its exception-report output feeds the cure/repurchase mechanic in Section 2.02(c); consistent.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c357","reasoning_cat1":"Parallel to (a) with a 180-day deadline; the 'appear defective on its face' standard again requires judgment but the mechanics are clear.","reasoning_cat2":"The Final Certification requires evidence of recording, yet Section 2.01 clause (x) expressly contemplates documents still out for recording, so the two must be reconciled in practice.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c358","reasoning_cat1":"The closing sentence says 'The obligation ... to cure, repurchase or substitute ... shall be the sole remedies respecting such defect available to the Certificateholders or to the Securities Administrator on their behalf' — a singular obligation described as plural 'remedies', and a sole-remedy clause whose reach ('such defect') is not defined.","reasoning_cat2":"It names only the Certificateholders and the Securities Administrator, omitting the Trustee, who is the party charged by Section 2.02(d) with enforcing repurchase obligations — so it is unclear whether the sole-remedy limitation binds the Trustee's enforcement action.","prob_cat1":0.42,"prob_cat2":0.44},
{"clause_id":"c359","reasoning_cat1":"A short but heavily loaded provision: it obliges the Trustee to enforce not only repurchase but 'any other obligations of the related Seller or the related Originator under such agreements, including, without limitation, the obligation of the Sponsor to repurchase ... any Mortgage Loan originated by Accredited in the event that Accredited fails' — a general catch-all followed by one named specific, leaving the backstop's scope and trigger ('fails to repurchase') open.","reasoning_cat2":"It has to be squared with Section 2.02(c)'s sole-remedy sentence, with the Purchase Price definition (c246) which covers only Section 2.02 repurchases, and with the repurchase machinery in the Mortgage Loan Purchase Agreement and Bring Down Agreements that this Agreement only incorporates by reference.","prob_cat1":0.56,"prob_cat2":0.55},
{"clause_id":"c360","reasoning_cat1":"The section is headed as the Master Servicer's and Securities Administrator's representations but its later paragraphs impose an unrelated notice-of-breach duty ('shall give prompt written notice thereof to the other parties') and the whole substitution and Purchase Price mechanic; 'prompt' and 'materially and adversely affects' are both open standards.","reasoning_cat2":"Several other provisions cite 'Section 2.03(b)(v)' (c200), 'Section 2.03(d)' (c241, c314) and 'the representations and warranties set forth in Section 2.03' (c280, c364) as if this section contained loan-level warranties and lettered subsections it does not have.","prob_cat1":0.40,"prob_cat2":0.47},
{"clause_id":"c361","reasoning_cat1":"A single-sentence survival clause; clear in itself.","reasoning_cat2":"It makes 'the representations and warranties set forth in Section 2.03' survive delivery of the Mortgage Loans, but Section 2.03's representations are Wells Fargo's corporate representations, which have nothing to do with delivery of Mortgage Files — and other provisions cite a non-existent Section 2.03(b)(v).","prob_cat1":0.17,"prob_cat2":0.40},
{"clause_id":"c362","reasoning_cat1":"Contains the ungrammatical 'Upon discovery by the Depositor, the Trustee of a breach' (missing conjunction), 'validly existing as limited liability company', and a mis-set subclause '(4)'; the good-title representation is otherwise clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Its notice duty runs to 'the other parties to this Agreement and to each Rating Agency', while the parallel duty in Section 2.03 omits the Rating Agencies — an unexplained asymmetry between two adjacent notice provisions.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c363","reasoning_cat1":"'Not in default or as to which default is not reasonably foreseeable' is a forward-looking standard, but the tax conditions it protects are precisely cited.","reasoning_cat2":"It opens 'Notwithstanding any contrary provision of this Agreement' and so overrides the repurchase timing in Sections 2.02 and 2.03, which is expressly acknowledged in Section 2.03's Purchase Price paragraph.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c364","reasoning_cat1":"Gives the Seller or Originator an option among cure, substitution and repurchase within 90 days; the mechanics are clear though 'discovery' is undefined.","reasoning_cat2":"It requires the Securities Administrator (not the Trustee) to reconvey the loan, while everywhere else the Custodian acts 'on behalf of the Trustee', and it points to substitution conditions 'in Section 2.03', which contains no lettered substitution conditions.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c365","reasoning_cat1":"An acknowledgement and declaration of trust; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 2.01's conveyance and Section 7.01's issuance of the Certificates.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c366","reasoning_cat1":"A conveyance in trust; the OCR renders 'REMIC II' inconsistently but the sense is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC II recital (c005) and c367.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.07},
{"clause_id":"c367","reasoning_cat1":"A conveyance in trust with a matched acknowledgement; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC III recital (c007) and the Class CE, P and IO Interest definitions.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c368","reasoning_cat1":"A conveyance in trust; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the REMIC IV definition (c270) and c107.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},

{"clause_id":"c371","reasoning_cat1":"The list is not grammatically parallel ('(a) acquire and hold' against '(b) to issue'), limb (d) is an open catch-all for anything 'necessary, suitable or convenient', and the final sentence trails off with 'and this Section 2.07'.","reasoning_cat2":"The purpose limitation has to be squared with the Trust's participation in the Swap and Yield Maintenance arrangements under Section 4.22, which are not among the enumerated purposes.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.22},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c378","reasoning_cat1":"A single short sentence; the qualifier 'if any' is loose but the disclaimer is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.03(b), under which the Master Servicer may step in as servicer, and with Section 8.03's limitations on liability.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c379","reasoning_cat1":"The bond and policy need only be 'in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees' — a standard with no ascertainable content and no minimum amount.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision fixes the coverage level, so the vagueness is not cured elsewhere; it sits alongside Section 8.03's liability limits.","prob_cat1":0.29,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c380","reasoning_cat1":"Grants power to do 'any and all things that it may deem necessary or desirable' followed by a non-exhaustive four-item list ('including but not limited to'), then a REMIC-protective proviso turning on what is 'reasonably within its control'.","reasoning_cat2":"It is subject to 'the provisions of Article XI' and Section 4.03, and its co-trustee limb points to Section 10.11; the discretion granted must be read against the Accepted Master Servicing Practices standard in Section 4.01.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.19},
{"clause_id":"c381","reasoning_cat1":"Almost wholly circular — every obligation is qualified by 'in accordance with this Agreement or the related Servicing Agreement', and the release limb is permissive ('may be released') without saying by whom or on what terms.","reasoning_cat2":"The substantive due-on-sale rules live in the Servicing Agreements, which are exhibits rather than operative text here, so this section supplies no independent standard.","prob_cat1":0.27,"prob_cat2":0.20},
{"clause_id":"c382","reasoning_cat1":"Long but procedurally concrete; the parenthetical 'or if the related Servicer does not, the Master Servicer may' creates a permissive backstop whose trigger is undefined.","reasoning_cat2":"It uses Exhibit G, the Request for Release form (c282), and interacts with Section 4.12's requirement that the Custodian retain Mortgage Files; consistent.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c383","reasoning_cat1":"The third sentence begins 'Such trust receipt shall obligate the related Servicer' although no trust receipt has been mentioned anywhere in the subsection — a dangling referent in the operative obligation to return the Mortgage File.","reasoning_cat2":"The document actually described is the Exhibit G request for release, and Section 4.12 requires the Custodian to retain each Mortgage File; the missing trust-receipt concept has to be supplied from the Custodial Agreements.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c384","reasoning_cat1":"Contains two broken constructions — 'The Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall provide access' (missing conjunction) and 'to the Trustee and, regarding the Mortgage Loans and their respective agents and accountants' — which obscure who is entitled to access.","reasoning_cat2":"A near-identical access regime already appears in Section 4.01 with different beneficiaries (Certificateholders, the FDIC and its examiners) and a different cost rule, so the two overlap imperfectly.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.26},
{"clause_id":"c385","reasoning_cat1":"Repeats the same missing conjunction ('the Master Servicer, the related Servicer shall be entitled to setoff') and grants a setoff right for amounts 'properly due and payable' without further definition.","reasoning_cat2":"The setoff right qualifies the declaration that the funds 'shall be and remain the sole and exclusive property of the Trustee', and must be squared with the permitted withdrawals in Sections 5.01 and 5.03.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c386","reasoning_cat1":"Refers to 'insurers meeting the eligibility requirements set forth in this Agreement and the related Servicing Agreement' and to a no-additional-insurance rule expressed by double negative; workable but not self-contained.","reasoning_cat2":"This Agreement does not itself set out insurer eligibility requirements anywhere — the Insurance Policy and LPMI Policy definitions only reference Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac standards for LPMI — so the cross-reference is to a standard that is not there.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c387","reasoning_cat1":"Procedurally clear, with an express carve-out for restoration amounts and a rule that added costs are ignored for distribution purposes.","reasoning_cat2":"It cites Sections 5.01 and 5.04 as the deposit authority and Sections 5.02, 5.03 or 5.04 for withdrawals, but the table of contents titles Section 5.04 the 'Yield Maintenance Credit Support Annex', which is not an account-withdrawal provision.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c388","reasoning_cat1":"Broad but bounded; 'such actions ... as shall be necessary to realize recovery' is a purposive standard with an illustrative list.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Insurance Proceeds definition (c166) and Section 4.11(b) on presenting claims.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c389","reasoning_cat1":"Uses the compound standard 'best reasonable efforts' and the awkward 'the Master Servicer, the related Servicer' construction again; the prohibitions themselves are clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Primary Mortgage Insurance Policy definition (c239) and the LPMI Policy definition; the nested 'to the extent required under this Agreement or the related Servicing Agreement' qualifiers make the obligation contingent on documents outside this instrument.","prob_cat1":0.21,"prob_cat2":0.18},
{"clause_id":"c390","reasoning_cat1":"Clear as to the duty to present claims; the deposit mechanic is stated plainly.","reasoning_cat2":"It directs deposit 'Pursuant to Sections 5.01 and 5.05', but this Agreement has no Section 5.05 — Article V ends at Section 5.04 — so the authority cited does not exist.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.37},
{"clause_id":"c391","reasoning_cat1":"'To the extent available' and 'until all amounts distributable ... have been distributed in full and the Master Servicer otherwise has fulfilled its obligations' are soft, but the custody duty is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Sections 2.02, 4.07 and the Custodial Agreements; the retention duty dovetails with the release mechanics in Section 4.07.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c392","reasoning_cat1":"'As come into and continue in default and as to which no satisfactory arrangements can be made for collection' is an open standard, and 'otherwise comparably convert' is a general catch-all after two specifics.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Liquidated Loan, Final Recovery Determination and REO Property definitions and Section 4.15.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c393","reasoning_cat1":"Clear in its components: the fee, float income, an expense-bearing rule and a Compensating Interest offset.","reasoning_cat2":"The float income is granted here, again in the Master Servicing Fee definition (c186) and again in Master Servicing Compensation (c185) — three provisions granting the same entitlement, which risks double counting in the Interest Funds calculation.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.31},
{"clause_id":"c394","reasoning_cat1":"'As expeditiously as possible' is an open timing standard; the REMIC foreclosure-property conditions are precisely cited.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.02's REMIC covenants and the REO Property and REO Imputed Interest definitions.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c395","reasoning_cat1":"One short sentence; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with the Protected Account definition (c245) and Section 4.15(d).","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c396","reasoning_cat1":"The proviso refers to 'any such unreimbursed Monthly Advances', a term this Agreement never defines and which does not match the 'Advances' referred to in the first half of the same sentence.","reasoning_cat2":"'Monthly Payment' and now 'Monthly Advances' are both undefined imports; the reimbursement priority also has to be read against the Liquidation Proceeds definition (c176), which already deducts unreimbursed Advances and Servicing Fees.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c397","reasoning_cat1":"'Net of any payment to the Master Servicer and the related Servicer as provided above' plus fixed deposit and remittance dates; clear.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c396, the Determination Date (c135) and Remittance Date (c276) definitions, both of which vary by Servicer.","prob_cat1":0.10,"prob_cat2":0.14},
{"clause_id":"c398","reasoning_cat1":"Long but concrete, save that it 'deems' non-compliance an Event of Default and then declares 'This paragraph shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary' — a sweeping override whose reach is not delimited.","reasoning_cat2":"The deemed Event of Default and the mandatory immediate termination sit against Section 9.01, which defines Events of Default and normally supplies cure periods, and against the Master Servicer's termination and successor provisions in Sections 8.05-8.06; the supersession clause is precisely the sort of override that has to be reconciled with the rest of the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c399","reasoning_cat1":"An intricate Regulation AB compliance regime with several nested 'to the extent' qualifiers, plus the same unbounded 'This paragraph shall supersede any other provision in this Agreement or any other agreement to the contrary'.","reasoning_cat2":"Like Section 4.16 it converts a reporting failure into an Event of Default with immediate termination, overriding Article IX; it also makes obligations depend on Exhibit N, which Section 4.17's own Servicing Criteria definition allows the parties to revise.","prob_cat1":0.28,"prob_cat2":0.39},

{"clause_id":"c401","reasoning_cat1":"Parallel to the Form 10-D regime and equally detailed; enumerators are again garbled and one deadline reads 'the 4 Business Day', but the scheme is workable.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c400 and Exhibit O; the Reportable Event definition (c281) points back here.","prob_cat1":0.19,"prob_cat2":0.14}

{"clause_id":"c378","reasoning_cat1":"A single short sentence; the qualifier 'if any' is loose but the disclaimer is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with Section 4.03(b), under which the Master Servicer may step in as servicer, and with Section 8.03's limitations on liability.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.09},

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c402","reasoning_cat1":"Long and dense, and it mis-cites itself: item (IV) refers to 'a Sarbanes-Oxley Certification as described in Section 4.18(a)(ii)(D) below' when the Sarbanes-Oxley Certification is set out in (a)(iii)(D), and the acknowledgement paragraph refers to duties 'under Sections 4.18(a)(iv) and (v)' rather than (a)(iii).","reasoning_cat2":"Its deliverables depend on Sections 4.16 and 4.17 and Exhibit O, and the discretion it gives the Securities Administrator to omit reports 'not required to be filed ... pursuant to Regulation AB' cuts against the mandatory delivery duties in those sections.","prob_cat1":0.30,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c403","reasoning_cat1":"Badly mangled: the opening list reads 'any Additional Form 10-D Disclosure, Additional Form 10- Disclosure or any Form 8-K Disclosure Information (collectively, the obligation to include such Additional Information ...' — the parenthetical that was meant to define 'Additional Disclosure' has been lost, and the notification sentence has the same four parties both giving and receiving the notice.","reasoning_cat2":"The Additional Disclosure definition (c022) says the term is 'As defined in Section 4.18', but the defining parenthetical is missing here, so a term used throughout Section 4.18 and Article I has no definition anywhere in the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.44,"prob_cat2":0.38},
{"clause_id":"c404","reasoning_cat1":"Procedurally detailed with clear allocations of responsibility and a carefully bounded liability carve-out; 'for any other reason' is broad but works in the party's favour.","reasoning_cat2":"Its closing rule that 'Fees and expenses incurred by the Securities Administrator in connection with this Section 4.18 shall not be reimbursable from the Trust Fund' sits against Sections 4.18(a)(i) and (iii), which make the Depositor responsible for such fees, and against the Trust-funded indemnity in Section 8.05.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.27},
{"clause_id":"c405","reasoning_cat1":"A conventional two-limb indemnity; the pronoun slip 'the Depositor and the Master Servicer and each of its officers' leaves the antecedent unclear, and the clarifying proviso is carefully drawn.","reasoning_cat2":"It parallels c406 and c407 and defines the Securities Administrator Information used by c295; consistent, though it overlaps with the Trust-level indemnity in Section 8.05.","prob_cat1":0.16,"prob_cat2":0.15},
{"clause_id":"c406","reasoning_cat1":"Parallel to c405 with the same structure; the enumerators are OCR-garbled but the sense is plain.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c405 and c407; the Depositor Information definition (c131) points back here.","prob_cat1":0.12,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c407","reasoning_cat1":"Parallel to c405 and c406; the first limb indemnifies both the Securities Administrator and the Depositor while the second limb runs only to the Depositor, an asymmetry that is probably deliberate but unexplained.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c405 and c406 and with the Master Servicer Information definition (c184).","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c408","reasoning_cat1":"Allocates contribution 'in such proportion as is appropriate to reflect the relative fault and the relative benefit of the respective parties' — a standard with no mechanism for determining either factor.","reasoning_cat2":"It is the fallback to c405-c407 and does not conflict with them, but no other provision supplies the missing determination mechanism.","prob_cat1":0.23,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c409","reasoning_cat1":"A single short survival sentence; determinate.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with c405-c408 and with the termination provisions of Article XI.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c410","reasoning_cat1":"Internally self-cancelling: the opening sentences make non-compliance an automatic Event of Default requiring immediate termination, while the closing sentence says 'Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, no Event of Default ... shall have occurred' where the failure stems from another party's late delivery — and the provision cites 'this Section 4.18(d)' although it sits in Section 4.18(b).","reasoning_cat2":"It duplicates, in almost identical words, the deemed-Event-of-Default and supersession paragraphs in Sections 4.16 and 4.17, and all three override Article IX's definition of Events of Default and the Master Servicer termination scheme in Sections 8.05-8.06.","prob_cat1":0.42,"prob_cat2":0.46},
{"clause_id":"c411","reasoning_cat1":"A single sentence; clear on its face.","reasoning_cat2":"It expressly displaces Section 12.01's amendment requirements for the whole of Section 4.18, joining the similar carve-out embedded in the Eligible Account definition (c143); the amendment regime is therefore fragmented across the instrument.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c412","reasoning_cat1":"Specifies an email address and telephone number; determinate, though 'may be delivered' leaves it permissive.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits alongside the general notice provision in Section 12.05, which this Section repeatedly cross-references; permissive rather than conflicting.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.12},
{"clause_id":"c413","reasoning_cat1":"Limb (b) requires the parties' obligations to be 'supplemented and modified as necessary to be consistent with any such amendments, interpretive advice or guidance, convention or consensus among active participants in the asset-backed securities markets, advice of counsel, or otherwise' — an open-ended, unascertainable source of obligation, and limb (a) is an express instruction on how to construe the Agreement.","reasoning_cat2":"Limb (d) declares that 'no amendment of this Agreement shall be required' to effect those changes, which cannot easily be reconciled with Section 12.01's amendment machinery or with the fixed deliverables and deadlines of Sections 4.16-4.18.","prob_cat1":0.44,"prob_cat2":0.42},
{"clause_id":"c414","reasoning_cat1":"A one-line obligation with no timing, no standard and no consequence, and it does not say for whose benefit the filings are made.","reasoning_cat2":"It places the duty on 'the Seller', a term covering two entities neither of which is a party to this Agreement, whereas the conveyance and perfection interests are the Trustee's under Section 2.01.","prob_cat1":0.26,"prob_cat2":0.30},
{"clause_id":"c415","reasoning_cat1":"Says 'This right may be assigned by the Seller to a third party' although the option is granted to Saxon or the Majority Class CE Certificateholder, not to the Seller; it also reinstates the option 'as of the first day of the related Fiscal Quarter' although the option is otherwise expressed without reference to quarters, and switches between 'Delinquent' and 'delinquent'.","reasoning_cat2":"The Purchase Price definition (c246) does expressly cover Section 4.21 purchases, but the Principal Funds definition (c241) attributes Section 4.21 repurchases to 'the related Originator, Saxon (or its assignee) or the Majority Class CE Certificateholder', a different cast of parties from the one named here.","prob_cat1":0.36,"prob_cat2":0.33}
]}
